full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader, J : This appeal at the instance of 44 plaintiffs directed against judgment and decree dated 23.07.2005 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Chittagong allowing application under Order VII Rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure thereby rejecting the plaint of Other Suit No. 65 of 2004 as barred under section 23 of Artha rin Adalat Ain 2003, Act 8 of 2003.

2. Plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit praying for decree as,-

“(ক) তপশীল সম্পত্তি এবং উহাতে স্থিত সকল গ্রহাদি বাদীগনের স্বত্বীয় ঘোষনার ডিক্রী দিতে।

(খ) তপশীল সম্পত্তিতে ১নং বিবাদীর কোন স্বত্ব সামিত নাই ছিল না মর্মে ঘোষনার ডিক্রী হয়।

(গ) তপশীল সম্পত্তি সম্পর্কে ৩নং বিবাদী বরাবরে ১নং বিবাদীর ০৬/০১/৯৬ ইংরেজী তারিখে সম্পাদিত কথিত এবং উক্ত তারিখে রেজিস্ট্রীকৃত ৩২ নম্বর যু্ক্ত বন্ধকী দলিল জাল, জালিয়াতি, ফেরবীও তঞ্চক এবং বাতিল ঘোষনার ডিক্রী হয়।

(ঘ) তপশীল সম্পত্তি সম্পর্কে ৩নং বিবাদীর বরাবরে ১নং বিবাদী কর্তৃক গত ০৬/০১/১৯৯৬ ইংরেজী তারিখে সম্পাদিত কথিত এবং উক্ত তারিখে রেজিষ্ট্রীকৃত ৩২নং বন্ধকী দলিল প্রদানের ১নং বিবাদীর কোন স্বত্ব সামিত্ব এবং অধীকার নাই মর্মে ঘোষনার ডিক্রী হয়।

3. The schedule of the suit is as follows:-

“মৌজা পশ্চিম নাছিরাবাদ, থানা-সবলমুরিং হাল পাহাড়তলী, জিলা-চট্রগ্রাম মহল ৭৫৯৮৬ তৌজি নং ২৪৩৮৩ আর, এসস, ২৬৮ নং খতিয়ানের আর, এস দাগ নং ৮০৪, ৮০৬, ৮২৭(সম্পূর্ন) পরিমান ৪১ শতক এবং আর, এস, ৩২২ নং খতিয়ানের আর,এস, দাগ নং ৮১৯,৮২১,৮২৮,৮৩০,৮৩১,৮০৫(সম্পূর্ন) পরিমান ১(এক) একর ০৭ শতক মোট পরিমান ১৪৮ শতক, সদৃশ পি,এস ২৯২/২৯৪ নং খতিয়ানের পি,এস, ৮০৪, ৮০৬, ৮২৭(সম্পূর্ন) এবং পি,এস ২৯৩/২৯৫ নং খতিয়ানের পি,এস  ৮১৯,৮২১,৮২৮,৮৩০,৮৩১,৮০৫(সম্পূর্ন বি,এস নামজারী খতিয়ান নং ৩৮৬ বি, এস, দাগ নং ৭৪২, ৭৪৯,৭৬৭,৭৬৯,৭৭৮,৭৭০,৭৭৯,৭৭৫,৭৭৬(সম্পূর্ন) পরিমান ১(এক)একর ৪৮ শতক পাউন্ডি, নাল, বাড়ী এবং সাই ভূমি এবং এই মোকদ্দমার খরচা বাবদ মবলগে অদ্য হইতে আদায়ের তারিখ তক শতকরা বার্ষিক টাকা হারে সুদ সহিত আদায় দেন।”

7. It appeals that suit was filed on 08.04.2008. Plaintiffs filed all the khatians and registered deeds along with plaint, plaintiffs also filed application under Order XXVI Rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure for inspection as to, whether the structures as mentioned in the plaint are situated in the suit land or not. Assistant Commissioner submitted report on 10.5.2002 finding that on the suit land there are structures of plaintiffs.

8. On 24.052005 defendant No. 3-4 i.e. Eastern Bank Limited and also Manager of Eastern Bank Limited filed application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In this application it is stated as:-

“বাদীপক্ষ তাহাদের মামলায় অর্থঋন আদালত আইন এর বিধাননুযায়ী অর্থঋন আদালত কর্তৃক অত্র বিবাদীগন কর্তৃক দায়েরকৃত এবং অত্র বিবাদীগনের পক্ষে বন্ধক মামলা ৩/০২ এ প্রচারিত রায়/ডিক্রীকে চ্যালেঞ্জ করিয়া এবং উক্ত রায়/ডিক্রীর অনুবলে দায়েরকৃত অর্থঋন জারী মামলা নং ২০/০৪ মূলে উক্ত বন্ধক মামলায় প্রচারিত ডিক্রীকে জারী কল্পে মাননীয় অর্থঋন আদালত কতৃক আইনানুযায়ী উক্ত বন্ধক মামলার বাদী অত্র বিবাদীগনের নিকট অত্র মামলার ২নং বিবাদী কর্তৃক বন্ধক কৃত সম্পত্তি উল্লেখিত জারী মামলার মাধ্যমে নিলাম বিক্রয়কে বাধাগ্রস্থ করার কু মানসে এবং অসৎ উদ্দেশ্যে অত্র মামলা আনায়ন করিয়াছে বিধায় অত্র মামলা আইনতঃ অচলও বারিত বিধায় মামলার আরজি খারিজ যোগ্য।

অর্থঋন আদালত আইন এর ২০ ধারানুযায়ী কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট অর্থঋন আদালতে বিচারাধীন কোন কার্যধারা বা উহার কোন আদেশ, রায় বা ডিক্রীর বিষয়ে কোন প্রশ্ন উৎত্থাপন করা যাইবে না এবং এই আইনের বিধানকে উপেক্ষা করিয়া কোন আদালতে বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট আবেদন করিয়া কোন প্রতিকার দাবী বা প্রার্থনা করা হইলে ঐ রুপ আবেদন কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষ গ্রাহ্য করিবে না।

আলোচ্যক্ষেত্রে ও বাদী পক্ষ অর্থঋন আদালত আইন এর ৩২ ধারানুযায়ী প্রতিকার দাবী করার সুযোগ থাকিলেও তাহাকে পাশ কাটাইয়া অত্র মামলা দায়ের করায় বাদীগনের মামলা আইনতঃ বারিত বিধায় বাদীর আইনতঃ সরাসরি খারিজযোগ্য।”

<u>9. Learned Judge took view that the suit is barred as per provision of section 23 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and plaintiffs could challenge the decree under section 32 of the said Ad. In rejecting the plaint, learned Judge relied on the decision of 44 DLR (AD) (1992) 260 wherein the Appellate Division held that, if any remedy is ordinarily available under both general law and special law, the remedy prescribed by the special law Must be sought in exclusion of the one available under the general law."</u>

10. Now, let us proceed with our judgment.

<u>11. This appeal the question calls for determination as to whether provision of Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable or not Learned Judge took view that the suit is clearly barred by special law, as such, the suit cannot proceed as special law provide remedy. It is to be mentioned that the application filed by defendant Nos. 2-3 did not specify under which provision/sub rule of rule 11 of Order VII the suit is barred but on a reading of the judgment it appears that learned Judge took the view that suit is barred under provision of sub rule (d) of rule 11 of Order VII wherein in the law is that plaint if barred by any law, it shall be rejected. It is settled by different decisions of the Appellate Division that if application does not specify under what provision of law, the application is made court is not bound to tress out the clause, fit the application with that clause and reject the plaint on taking into consideration of the facts of the case.</u>

<u>12. On a reading of the relief claimed in the suit, we have seen that plaintiffs did not challenge the decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 03 of 2002. If we consider the case of defendant in its true perspective then best case for defendant No. 3 and 4 is that suit is barred by law. The plaintiffs are 3rd party as they are not in any manner or in any form before the Artha Rin Adalat. Let us tee what are the remedies available to a 3rd party who is stranger to the proceeding or whether any remedy provide to a stranger or 3rd party of a suit of Artha Rin Adalat. As per section 6(5) of the Act, the presence of 3rd party can be seen as mortgagor or guarantor i.e. they in this and that forum are within the frame of the suit i.e. these two categories of 3rd party in framing of the suit in any forum be before the Adalat  as such these two categories of 3rd  party are not stranger to the suit or proceeding. Section 32(1) provides for filing objection by 1st  party, without specifying whether mortgagor or guarantor against execution proceeding without going for further litigation against debtor. Section 32(2) if read with Section 6(5) then it only fix either mortgagor or guarantor, not any stranger as they are not involve in the matter in any capacity. Section 36(1) of the Act relating to a stranger 3rd party where this 3rd party stranger has given relief for realising money from the debtor through the execution proceeding. In the instant case- 44 plaintiffs have filed the suit primarily for a decree of title as their properties were given mortgage by a single person and according to the plaintiffs, this single person has no title over the mortgage property. Artha Rin Adalat no where provide for deciding title which is the jurisdiction of civil court alone. It is the settled principle of law that plaint is to be rejected only on reference to the plaint or on reading of the plaint if it is found that plaint has come within any of the sub-rule of rule 11 of order VII of the Code then the plaint 'shall' be rejected. It may be said that on a meaningful, not formal, reading of the plaint if it is manifestly vexations and meritless, not disclosing a clear right to sue, then in exercise of Rule 11 of Order VII of the Code , taking care of the ground mentioned therein is fulfilled, plaint can be rejected. In the instant suit plaint does not disclose any such defect to be throttled before born.</u>

13. Learned Judge took the view that suit is barred as per section 20 of the Act.

14. From the discussion made herein above we are of the view that this provision of law has been misapplied by the learned Judge because Artha Rin Adalat is vested with pleanary jurisdiction for realising money of the financial institutions, it has no jurisdiction to decide title of the land involved in the suit. It is special law for limited purpose. Section 20 of the Act relates to parties to the suit, section 32 relates to stranger, who has a claim over the money, nothing more, nothing less. It is seen from the Commissioner's report that plaintiffs possessing the suit land. It is also seen that plaintiffs constructed even 5 storied buildings over the suit land before mortgage given by defendant No. 1. It also appears that plaintiffs mortgaged the schedule property to different financial institutions and repay the loan. It appears that some documents have been produced by hand from Bank relating to the suit land, clause 10 of the mortgage deed empower the Bank official to inspect the mortgage property, which from the foregoing fact, has not been done as if the Bank official inspect the mortgaged land then they would certainly found that defendant No.1 did not possess the mortgaged land, rather as per Advocate Commissioner's report, plaintiffs' possession would be found. Section 20 of the Act cannot be invoked by a stranger, it only relates to the parties to the suit.

15. Learned Judge was of the opinion that plaintiffs can get remedy under section 32 of the Act. Section 32 of the Act is as follows:-

“অর্থঋন আদালতের ডিক্রী বা আদেশ হইতে উদ্ভুত জারী মামলায় কোন তৃতীয় পক্ষ দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির আইনের বিধানমতে দাবী পেশ করিলে, আদালত প্রাথমিক বিবেচনায় উক্ত দাবী সরাসরি খারিজ না করিলে, ডিক্রীদার অনুর্ধ ৩০(ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে উহার বিরুদ্ধে লিখিত আপত্তি দায়ের করিয়া শুনানী দাবী করিতে পারিবেন।”

(২)উপধারা মতে দাবী পেশ করিবার ক্ষেত্রে, দরখাস্তকারী, ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের অথবা ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থের আংশিক ইতিমধ্যে আদায় হইয়া থাকিলে অনাদায়ী অংশের, ১০এর সমপরিমান জামানত বা বন্ড দাখিল করিবে এবং অনুরুপ জামানত বা বন্ড দাখিল না করিলে উক্ত দাবী অগ্রাহ্য হইবে।

16. It is true that stranger 3rd party could came before the court under this Act but it appears that 10% of decreetal amount ought to be deposited but this provision is not applicable to the plaintiffs as the suit was filed for declaration of title. Even though, why plaintiffs would pay such huge amount of money as plaintiffs case is that they did not mortgaged the property and when 44 plaintiffs are owner of the property, how a single person could mortgage the entire property. As such, the facts of the instant suit requires evidence as per Order X of the Code to settle the dispute. When evidence is required then trial is to commence and when trial is required, plaint can not be rejected.

<u>17. The learned Judge rejected the plaint taking view that there is complete ouster of jurisdiction of Civil Court. We have also seen that plaintiffs are neither loanee nor mortgagor but their property was given mortgage by defendant No. 1 of which defendant No. 1 has no title. Plaintiffs chosen their forum as they cannot invoke the jurisdiction of Artha  Rin Adalat as plaintiffs do not fall any of the category of the parties who can invoke jurisdiction of Artha Rin Adalat. On the question of jurisdiction one must refer to the substance of the matter and not to the forum of the suit. But to find out the jurisdiction of the court it is to be looked in to as to whether relief claimed by the plaintiffs can be awarded by the court. If plaintiffs can established the facts then plaintiffs can get relief from forum chose otherwise the suit would be dismissed. Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure empowered civil court to entertain suit of civil nature. The fact of each of the suit, speaks whether civil court has jurisdiction or not. Artha Rin Adalat Ain as special statute provided special measure to the parties who can invoke provision of the Act. Under Artha Rin Adalat Ain only financial institutions can institute a suit against loanee and guarantor or mortgagor not anyone for realizing money and not to decide any other claim. It has been established that civil courts have jurisdiction to see if the statutory authority has acted in conformity with the provisions of the statute. Civil courts have always the jurisdiction to determine whether a court of special jurisdiction is acting in accordance with law or within the limits prescribed by law or in conformity with the fundamental principles of judicial procedure as such determination in. effect amounts to determining the extent to which the jurisdiction of the civil court is ousted. It is well settled that ouster of jurisdiction is of no avail in case of coram non judice or without jurisdiction or where the provisions of the Act containing the ouster clause have not been complied with, In the case of I3angladesh Shilpa Rin Sangshtha-Vs-Rahman Textile Mills Ltd and others, 51 DLR (AD) 221 majority view is that suit having been filed before civil court cannot proceed but the minority view which according to me took correct view held as,-</u>

<u>"Plaints and the prayers of both the suits show that the plaintiffs have disowned liability of loan alleging re-payment of the same by the BTMC on their behalf and asserted that the properties concerned were not mortgaged or hypothecated with the Sangstha and that the action taken by the Sangstha was malafide. It has to be noticed that there has been no provision for appeal or no forum provided in the Order for redress of genuine grievances of anybody or person when injustice is perpetrated on them. It cannot be imagined that such a body or person should be precluded from receiving assistance from a Court of law, Civil Court is a Court of ultimate jurisdiction, and in cases where no other remedy is provided for, the door of the civil court should not be closed and hermetically sealed against one who has been subjected to injustice. In the view I have taken of the legal position I am constrained to find hat in the instant case the civil Court has jurisdiction to entertain the plaints. The correctness of the allegations can be resolved only at the trial."</u>

18. Similar view as taken by the minority that majority view also get support from the case of Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Sangstha-Vs-Azir Uddin Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 96 and also from the case of Delwar Coil Foam Industries Ltd vs. Bangladesh Shilpa Rin Shangstha and others, 1991 BLD 317. In the case of blur Mohammed vs. M. Ahmed 39 DLR (AD) 1 it is held that "This is a well-known proposition of law which this court has yet no occasion to depart from or express any disagreement with it. The point, however, it whether any bar of suit imposed by the legislature can be disregarded to make such suit, which is so barred, maintainable in order to try an issue on malafide alleged M the plaint, it may, at least in some cases, be seen that hardship, or even injustice, may result if, in spite of evident truth in the allegation of male fide, the suit is held to be not maintainable because there is a bar against such suit in the statute concerned, But, seeker of justice in a court of law should become aware, if not already so, that justice is done according to law. A Judge may have sympathy for a litigant's suffering due to technicalities of law made by the legislature still in view of the express legislative intention, he must follow the hands-off doctrine. Otherwise chaos and anarchy would prevail leading to all sorts of complexities and confusion. Whatever the legislature says unless it is contrary to Constitution, its mandate, either express or implied, has been beyond by Court."

19. So far, we have seen the financial institutions disbursing huge loans against mortgage without any spot verification and loosing huge public money. If it is found that loan against mortgage has been disburse to a wrong title less person then the money shall be realised from the persons who involved in disbursing the money.

20. We find merit in the appeal.

21. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs.

22. Judgment complained is set aside. Other Class Suit No. 65 of 2004 is to be proceeded legally.
